From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Initial payload latency and streaming handoff - post-demo checklist

Hi Sam — great demo earlier today, thanks for the time. Quick recap of the SLA/behavior items we agreed to validate and the immediate next steps so nothing falls through the cracks:

Key performance targets you called out:
- Primary TTFT targets: median <= 300ms, p95 <= 600ms for typical single-request flows (350 tokens avg).
- Streaming behavior: prefer Server-Sent Events (SSE) for browser clients; chunk cadence should feel progressive (rough guideline: initial chunk within 200-300ms, subsequent chunks every ~120-300ms depending on model tokenization).
- Throughput/concurrency: pilot expected peak ~80 QPS with ~200 concurrent active sessions in peak 10-min windows.

What we (Redwood) will deliver for the pilot:
- Demo recording + initial SLO proposal attached.
- A 2-week pilot harness (perf script + synthetic traffic) to validate TTFT and throughput under realistic token distributions.
- A short checklist we need from ClearPay: sample request shapes (avg/95th token counts), preferred client transport (SSE vs WebSocket), compliance/data residency constraints.

Immediate asks for ClearPay:
1) Confirm that median <= 300ms and p95 <= 600ms are acceptable guardrails for the pilot, or propose adjustments.
2) Share the sample request distribution (CSV is fine) and any region/KMS requirements.
3) Preferred pilot start window (we suggested next week).

Attachments: demo-recording-20260831.mp4, initial-slo-proposal-clearpay.pdf

If you confirm the targets, we’ll spin up the harness and propose a canary plan (5% traffic -> 25% -> full pilot) and a telemetry dashboard (median/p95 TTFT, token throughput, GPU util, tail latencies).

Thanks —
Aditya Rao

Thanks Aditya — good summary. A few notes from our side after we synced with engineering and product: 

- The median <= 300ms is fine; for p95 we want some slack during heavy bursts — can you validate to an initial target of p95 <= 800ms? If we see clear room for improvement during the pilot we can tighten to 600ms.
- Throughput: the 80 QPS peak and ~200 concurrent sessions sound accurate based on our user projections. Important: many sessions will use longer chat histories (up to ~700 tokens trimmed in context) which may affect actual per-request token counts.
- Transport: browser product team prefers SSE for simplicity, but we are open to using WebSocket for mobile clients if there’s a measurable TTFT benefit.

Next steps for us:
1) I’ll attach a small sample CSV of request lengths and 90-day traffic profile (send separately if needed).
2) We’ll need a short checklist documenting what network egress IPs to allow and any KMS/data-residency constraints.
3) Pilot timing: aiming for week of Sep 7 if Redwood can confirm readiness.

On the p95 ask: please include a run with synthetic longer-history requests in the pilot so we can see tail behavior.

Hi Sam — looping in a short technical plan and clarifications from our infra side. Thanks for the clarification about longer histories; that will definitely influence both batching behavior and KV cache pressure.

Technical clarifications & suggestions:
- Transport: SSE is fine for browser clients and simplifies proxies. For the lowest TTFT we typically recommend WebSocket for streaming (fewer re-connect costs and lower header overhead), but we can configure SSE with optimized chunking and keep-alive to achieve comparable first-chunk timings. We’ll include both options in the pilot.
- Chunk cadence: propose baseline profile for pilot -> initial chunk target <= 250ms, then 100-200ms cadence for subsequent chunks for the first 1–2s of generation; after that cadence can relax depending on model throughput. We’ll expose cadence knobs in the harness so you can tune client pacing.
- Batching & concurrency: to hit median TTFT targets we’ll instrument a continuous-batching policy tuned to typical request token sizes. For 80 QPS / 200 concurrent, initial config: per-GPU max concurrency 48, dynamic batch cap 32 tokens/batch, prefer max-batch-window 25ms. We’ll adjust during pilot to balance tail and median.
- KV cache & longer context: we recommend using prefix-KV caching for repeated user histories; we’ll test both cold and warmed cache scenarios in the pilot. Please include representative proportions of cold vs warmed sessions in the CSV.

Pilot plan (2 weeks):
- Week 1: synthetic perf runs (varying token lengths: 100, 350, 700) + determine baseline TTFT and p95.
- Week 2: limited-canary with progressively real traffic (5% -> 25% -> 100% of pilot traffic) and telemetry dashboard.

Metrics we’ll publish to your dashboard:
- Median TTFT, p95 TTFT, median token throughput, GPU utilization, request QPS, tail time spent in batching queue.

Attachments: pilot-harness-instructions.md (link and attached), we also shared a Drive folder with the pilot config: https://drive.redwood.com/clearpay/pilot-plan-CP-2026-08-31

If these items look good we’ll provision the pilot environment and send an access checklist (egress IPs, webhook endpoints, DocuSign NDA if required).

Ben Carter
